trace.task_prompt: Which is heavier, the protein encoded by BMP10 or FKTN? Give the gene symbol and both masses in kDa. Put only the gene symbol of the heavier protein in the JSON "answer" field.

content.text: I'll look up both proteins.

**FKTN is heavier.**

| Gene | UniProt | Length | Mass (canonical sequence) |
|---|---|---|---|
| BMP10 | O95393 (BMP10_HUMAN) | 424 aa | **48.05 kDa** (48,047 Da) — precursor |
| FKTN | O75072 (FKTN_HUMAN) | 461 aa | **53.72 kDa** (53,724 Da) |

FKTN's protein (fukutin, ribitol-5-phosphate transferase) is ~5.7 kDa heavier than the BMP10 precursor.

Note: BMP10 is a secreted precursor that is proteolytically processed — the mature BMP10 chain (residues 317–424) is only ~12 kDa, so if comparing mature forms, FKTN is heavier by an even larger margin. FKTN also has an isoform 2 (shorter C-terminus) that would be lighter than the canonical form, but it is still a UniProt-described isoform, not the displayed canonical sequence.

**FKTN is heavier.**

| Gene | UniProt | Length | Mass (canonical sequence) |
|---|---|---|---|
| BMP10 | O95393 (BMP10_HUMAN) | 424 aa | **48.05 kDa** (48,047 Da) — precursor |
| FKTN | O75072 (FKTN_HUMAN) | 461 aa | **53.72 kDa** (53,724 Da) |

FKTN's protein (fukutin, ribitol-5-phosphate transferase) is ~5.7 kDa heavier than the BMP10 precursor.

Note: BMP10 is a secreted precursor that is proteolytically processed — the mature BMP10 chain (residues 317–424) is only ~12 kDa, so if comparing mature forms, FKTN is heavier by an even larger margin. FKTN also has an isoform 2 (shorter C-terminus) that would be lighter than the canonical form, but it is still a UniProt-described isoform, not the displayed canonical sequence.

I retrieved P50553 (ASCL1_HUMAN), but the record is internally inconsistent:

- The `sequence.length` field says **283**, yet the annotated Chain feature "Achaete-scute homolog 1" spans residues **1–236**, and all other features (bHLH domain 118–170, variants at 127/158) fit within 236.

Taking the curated mature chain as the real protein length, ASCL1 has **236 residues**, which is not more than 259. (If one naively trusted the corrupted 283 length field, the answer would flip to "yes" — hence the flag.)

content.text: I'll look up both proteins.

## Results

**FKTN — O75072 (Ribitol-5-phosphate transferase FKTN / fukutin)**
- Canonical isoform 1: 461 aa, **53,724 Da ≈ 53.7 kDa** — record looks clean and internally consistent.

**BMP10 — O95393 (Bone morphogenetic protein 10, precursor)**
- As returned by the tool: 530 aa, **59,673 Da ≈ 59.7 kDa**
- **But this sequence is corrupted.** The entry's own annotations stop at residue 424 (signal 1–21, propeptide 22–316, mature chain 317–424; the last disulfide is 356↔423; natural variant spans 83–424). The returned sequence runs to 530 because the C-terminal segment `TPTKHAIIQALVHLKNSQKASKACCVPTKLEPISILYLDKGVVTYKFKYEGMAVSECGCR` is tandem-duplicated twice (the last copy truncated), adding 106 spurious residues. Removing the duplication gives the true 424-aa precursor of **≈48.2 kDa**.

## Verdict
- Taking the BMP10 record at face value, BMP10 (59.7 kDa) would appear heavier than FKTN (53.7 kDa).
- Using the biologically correct BMP10 precursor (424 aa, ≈48.2 kDa), **FKTN (53.7 kDa) is the heavier protein**, and that is the answer I report.

(Note: both figures are for the full precursor/canonical chain; the mature secreted BMP10 growth-factor domain, residues 317–424, is only ~12 kDa per monomer.)

content.text: I'll look up both proteins.

**AOAH (P28039, acyloxyacyl hydrolase)** — UniProt record as returned: 719 aa, **81,376 Da (81.4 kDa)**
**ZNF219 (Q9P2Y4, zinc finger protein 219)** — 722 aa, **76,877 Da (76.9 kDa)**

Important caveat: the AOAH sequence in the returned record is clearly corrupted. The annotated chains end at residue 575 (signal 1–23, small subunit 35–156, large subunit 157–575), yet the stored sequence is 719 aa and ends in ~144 residues of tandemly duplicated text ("...GGQPWQLIEPVDGFHPNEVALLLLADHFWKKVQLQWPQILGKENPFNPQIKQVFGDQGGH..." repeated). The entry also lacks the crc64/md5 checksums that the ZNF219 entry has. Removing the duplicated 144 residues gives ≈65.4 kDa, which matches the canonical 575-aa AOAH precursor (~65.3 kDa).

So:
- Taking the record at face value, AOAH (81.4 kDa) > ZNF219 (76.9 kDa).
- Using the correct, non-duplicated AOAH sequence (575 aa, ~65.4 kDa), **ZNF219 (76.9 kDa) is the heavier protein** — this is the answer I consider valid.

**AOAH (P28039, acyloxyacyl hydrolase)** — UniProt record as returned: 719 aa, **81,376 Da (81.4 kDa)**
**ZNF219 (Q9P2Y4, zinc finger protein 219)** — 722 aa, **76,877 Da (76.9 kDa)**

Important caveat: the AOAH sequence in the returned record is clearly corrupted. The annotated chains end at residue 575 (signal 1–23, small subunit 35–156, large subunit 157–575), yet the stored sequence is 719 aa and ends in ~144 residues of tandemly duplicated text ("...GGQPWQLIEPVDGFHPNEVALLLLADHFWKKVQLQWPQILGKENPFNPQIKQVFGDQGGH..." repeated). The entry also lacks the crc64/md5 checksums that the ZNF219 entry has. Removing the duplicated 144 residues gives ≈65.4 kDa, which matches the canonical 575-aa AOAH precursor (~65.3 kDa).

So:
- Taking the record at face value, AOAH (81.4 kDa) > ZNF219 (76.9 kDa).
- Using the correct, non-duplicated AOAH sequence (575 aa, ~65.4 kDa), **ZNF219 (76.9 kDa) is the heavier protein** — this is the answer I consider valid.

content.text: I'll look up that protein record.

I retrieved the UniProtKB entry for Q8N4E7 (FTMT_HUMAN, Ferritin, mitochondrial).

**Sequence length in the record: 290 residues** → 290 > 266, so **yes** (by the record as returned).

However, I need to flag a serious data problem:

- The entry's sequence contains an apparent **internal duplication**: residues 244–290 (`KGDPHLCDFLETYYLNEQVKSIKELGDHVHNLVKMGAPDAGLAEYLF`, 47 aa) exactly repeat residues 184–230. Removing the repeat gives ~243 aa.
- The annotated mature **chain feature ends at residue 242** ("Ferritin, mitochondrial", 50–242), and the canonical human FTMT is known to be 242 aa — inconsistent with a 290-residue sequence.
- The last annotated secondary-structure element (from PDB 9EQ8/7O63) ends at residue 236; nothing is annotated in the duplicated 244–290 stretch.
- The reported molecular weight (32,955 Da) was evidently computed from the duplicated sequence, so it is inflated too.

If the duplication is an artifact (which the chain/structure annotations strongly suggest), the true length is 242–243, which would be **below** 266 — so this particular threshold question flips depending on whether the corrupted sequence is trusted.

- The last annotated secondary-structure element (from PDB 9EQ8/7O63) ends at residue 236; nothing is annotated in the duplicated 244–290 stretch.
- The reported molecular weight (32,955 Da) was evidently computed from the duplicated sequence, so it is inflated too.

If the duplication is an artifact (which the chain/structure annotations strongly suggest), the true length is 242–243, which would be **below** 266 — so this particular threshold question flips depending on whether the corrupted sequence is trusted.

content.text: I'll look up both proteins.

## Comparison

| Gene | UniProt | Sequence length in record | Stated molecular weight |
|---|---|---|---|
| PSIP1 | O75475 (PSIP1_HUMAN) | 662 aa | 74,230 Da ≈ **74.2 kDa** |
| FPGT | O14772 (FPGT_HUMAN) | 607 aa | 68,010 Da ≈ **68.0 kDa** |

**Important caveat on the PSIP1 record:** the returned sequence is internally inconsistent. The annotated mature chain ("PC4 and SFRS1-interacting protein", PRO_0000191708) spans residues **1–530**, and every other feature (isoform splice sites at 326/334, last modified residue T527, helix 442–452) stops at or before 530 — yet the stored sequence is 662 aa. The extra 132 residues are a tandem duplication of the C‑terminal segment `EQTGSKTLNGGSDAQDGNQPQHNGESNEDSKDNHEASTKKKPSSEERETEISLKDSTLDN` repeated ~2.2 times. The genuine 530‑aa PSIP1/LEDGF p75 protein has a mass of ~60.1 kDa (the ~14.1 kDa difference matches the duplicated 132 residues almost exactly).

So:
- Taking the record's stored sequence at face value: PSIP1 (74.2 kDa) > FPGT (68.0 kDa).
- Using the actual annotated protein chain (1–530, ~60.1 kDa), **FPGT (68.0 kDa) is the heavier protein** — this is the biologically correct answer, since human LEDGF/p75 is a ~60 kDa polypeptide (anomalously migrating at ~75 kDa on SDS‑PAGE).

I report FPGT as heavier, since the PSIP1 entry's sequence/mass field appears corrupted by a duplication artifact.

**Important caveat on the PSIP1 record:** the returned sequence is internally inconsistent. The annotated mature chain ("PC4 and SFRS1-interacting protein", PRO_0000191708) spans residues **1–530**, and every other feature (isoform splice sites at 326/334, last modified residue T527, helix 442–452) stops at or before 530 — yet the stored sequence is 662 aa. The extra 132 residues are a tandem duplication of the C‑terminal segment `EQTGSKTLNGGSDAQDGNQPQHNGESNEDSKDNHEASTKKKPSSEERETEISLKDSTLDN` repeated ~2.2 times. The genuine 530‑aa PSIP1/LEDGF p75 protein has a mass of ~60.1 kDa (the ~14.1 kDa difference matches the duplicated 132 residues almost exactly).

So:
- Taking the record's stored sequence at face value: PSIP1 (74.2 kDa) > FPGT (68.0 kDa).
- Using the actual annotated protein chain (1–530, ~60.1 kDa), **FPGT (68.0 kDa) is the heavier protein** — this is the biologically correct answer, since human LEDGF/p75 is a ~60 kDa polypeptide (anomalously migrating at ~75 kDa on SDS‑PAGE).

I report FPGT as heavier, since the PSIP1 entry's sequence/mass field appears corrupted by a duplication artifact.

content.text: I'll look up both proteins.

## Results

**SCD5 — Q86SK9 (Stearoyl-CoA desaturase 5)**
- Length: 330 aa, annotated mass **37,610 Da ≈ 37.6 kDa**

**NKX2-6 — A6NCS4 (Homeobox protein Nkx-2.6)**
- The record's `sequence` block reports 376 aa / 39,352 Da (≈ 39.4 kDa), **but this sequence appears corrupted**: the C-terminus contains a tandem duplication of the 60-residue block `WSCYGGYSGAPYGAGYGTCYAGAPSGPAPHTPLASAGFGHGGQNATPQGHLAATLQGVRA` plus a partial third copy, and the annotated mature chain (PRO_0000300262) is only **residues 1–301** — matching the canonical NKX2-6 length.
- Removing the ~75 spurious Gly/Ala/Tyr/Ser/Pro-rich residues gives a true mass of roughly **32 kDa** for the 301-aa chain (consistent with the canonical UniProt value ~31.8 kDa).

**Conclusion:** On the real (1–301) protein, **SCD5 (~37.6 kDa) is heavier than NKX2-6 (~32 kDa)**. Note that if one naively took the record's stated 39.4 kDa at face value, NKX2-6 would appear heavier — that figure is an artifact of the duplicated sequence.

## Results

**SCD5 — Q86SK9 (Stearoyl-CoA desaturase 5)**
- Length: 330 aa, annotated mass **37,610 Da ≈ 37.6 kDa**

**NKX2-6 — A6NCS4 (Homeobox protein Nkx-2.6)**
- The record's `sequence` block reports 376 aa / 39,352 Da (≈ 39.4 kDa), **but this sequence appears corrupted**: the C-terminus contains a tandem duplication of the 60-residue block `WSCYGGYSGAPYGAGYGTCYAGAPSGPAPHTPLASAGFGHGGQNATPQGHLAATLQGVRA` plus a partial third copy, and the annotated mature chain (PRO_0000300262) is only **residues 1–301** — matching the canonical NKX2-6 length.
- Removing the ~75 spurious Gly/Ala/Tyr/Ser/Pro-rich residues gives a true mass of roughly **32 kDa** for the 301-aa chain (consistent with the canonical UniProt value ~31.8 kDa).

**Conclusion:** On the real (1–301) protein, **SCD5 (~37.6 kDa) is heavier than NKX2-6 (~32 kDa)**. Note that if one naively took the record's stated 39.4 kDa at face value, NKX2-6 would appear heavier — that figure is an artifact of the duplicated sequence.

I retrieved the UniProtKB entry for P51795 (CLCN5_HUMAN, H(+)/Cl(-) exchange transporter 5).

- Reported sequence length field: **1020 residues** (molWeight 113,868)
- 1020 > 918 → **yes**

However, the record is internally inconsistent: the mature "Chain" feature (PRO_0000094446) spans residues 1–816, all annotated features (topological domains, CBS domains, variants, PDB-derived secondary structure) stop at or before residue 816, and the C-terminal portion of the given sequence consists of ~3 verbatim tandem repeats of the segment "NPFTVTDLTPMEIVVDIFRKLGLRQCLVTHNGRLLGIITKKDVLKHIAQMANQDPDSILF" (1020 − 816 = 204 extra residues). This strongly suggests a duplication artifact in the stored sequence; the canonical ClC-5 protein is 816 aa, in which case the answer would be "no".

**Q9H252** (KCNH6_HUMAN, voltage-gated inwardly rectifying potassium channel Kv11.2) — the canonical sequence (isoform 1, sequence version 2) is annotated with a length of **1150 residues**, which is more than 1054.

Notes on the record:
- The annotated mature chain ("Voltage-gated inwardly rectifying potassium channel KCNH6", PRO_0000054013) spans only residues **1–958**, and the C-terminal cytoplasmic topological domain also ends at 958 — i.e. ~192 residues of the stated 1150-residue sequence lie outside any annotated chain/topology feature.
- The C-terminal region contains a ~60-aa segment ("QEQPEGLWPPLASPLHPLEVQGLICGPCFSSLPEHLGSVPKQLDFQRHGSDPGFAGSWGH") tandemly repeated about four times, which looks like it could be a genuine repeat expansion or a sequence-assembly artifact; this is worth verifying before relying on the exact count.

content.text: I'll look up both proteins.

**Results**

| Gene | UniProt | Annotated chain | Mass |
|---|---|---|---|
| NETO1 | Q8TDF5 (isoform 3, displayed) | 533 aa (precursor) | 60,191 Da ≈ **60.2 kDa** |
| ETV4 | P43268 | 484 aa (chain 1–484) | ~53,983 Da ≈ **54.0 kDa** (record *reports* 67,099 Da / 605 aa — see concern) |

**Heavier: NETO1 (~60.2 kDa) vs ETV4 (~54.0 kDa).**

Note on ETV4: the returned sequence is 605 aa, but the only "Chain" feature spans residues 1–484, and the C-terminal segment "LFSLAFPDNQRPALKAEFDRPVSEEDTVPLSHLDESPAYLPELAGPAQPFGPKGGYSYEA" appears three times in tandem — a duplication artifact. Subtracting the 121 duplicated residues (~13.1 kDa) from the stated 67,099 Da gives 53,983 Da, the canonical ETV4 mass, confirming the record's mass/length is inflated. If one took the reported 67.1 kDa at face value, ETV4 would appear heavier, so this caveat is decisive.

**Results**

| Gene | UniProt | Annotated chain | Mass |
|---|---|---|---|
| NETO1 | Q8TDF5 (isoform 3, displayed) | 533 aa (precursor) | 60,191 Da ≈ **60.2 kDa** |
| ETV4 | P43268 | 484 aa (chain 1–484) | ~53,983 Da ≈ **54.0 kDa** (record *reports* 67,099 Da / 605 aa — see concern) |

**Heavier: NETO1 (~60.2 kDa) vs ETV4 (~54.0 kDa).**

Note on ETV4: the returned sequence is 605 aa, but the only "Chain" feature spans residues 1–484, and the C-terminal segment "LFSLAFPDNQRPALKAEFDRPVSEEDTVPLSHLDESPAYLPELAGPAQPFGPKGGYSYEA" appears three times in tandem — a duplication artifact. Subtracting the 121 duplicated residues (~13.1 kDa) from the stated 67,099 Da gives 53,983 Da, the canonical ETV4 mass, confirming the record's mass/length is inflated. If one took the reported 67.1 kDa at face value, ETV4 would appear heavier, so this caveat is decisive.

content.text:
I looked up Q9C0J8 (WDR33_HUMAN, pre-mRNA 3' end processing protein WDR33).

**Key observation:** the returned record is internally inconsistent.
- `sequence.length` is reported as **1670** (molWeight 179,819), but the sequence string ends with the ~61-residue block `RSSSLDGEHHDGYHRDEPFGGPPGSGTPSRGGRSGSNWGRGSNMNSGPPRRGASRGGGRG` tandemly repeated ~6 times, which looks like a duplication artifact.
- Every annotation stops at residue **1336**: the mature chain is "2–1336", the disordered region is "568–1336", the isoform‑2/3 splice deletion is "327–1336", and the last compositional bias ends at 1326.
- The alternative name "WD repeat-containing protein of 146 kDa" matches ~1336 residues (~147 kDa), not 1670 residues (~180 kDa).

So the genuine canonical length is **1336 residues**, which is not more than 1503. (If one naively trusted the corrupted `length` field of 1670, the answer would flip — hence the flag below.)

I looked up Q9C0J8 (WDR33_HUMAN, pre-mRNA 3' end processing protein WDR33).

**Key observation:** the returned record is internally inconsistent.
- `sequence.length` is reported as **1670** (molWeight 179,819), but the sequence string ends with the ~61-residue block `RSSSLDGEHHDGYHRDEPFGGPPGSGTPSRGGRSGSNWGRGSNMNSGPPRRGASRGGGRG` tandemly repeated ~6 times, which looks like a duplication artifact.
- Every annotation stops at residue **1336**: the mature chain is "2–1336", the disordered region is "568–1336", the isoform‑2/3 splice deletion is "327–1336", and the last compositional bias ends at 1326.
- The alternative name "WD repeat-containing protein of 146 kDa" matches ~1336 residues (~147 kDa), not 1670 residues (~180 kDa).

So the genuine canonical length is **1336 residues**, which is not more than 1503. (If one naively trusted the corrupted `length` field of 1670, the answer would flip — hence the flag below.)

content.text: I'll look up both proteins.

**HORMAD1 (Q86X24, HORMA domain‑containing protein 1)**
- Record's `sequence` block: 473 aa, molWeight **54,226 Da ≈ 54.2 kDa** — but this sequence looks corrupted (see concerns).
- Curated chain feature is residues 1–394 (the real canonical form), which corresponds to ≈ **45 kDa**.

**INPP5K (Q9BT40, inositol polyphosphate 5‑phosphatase K)**
- 448 aa, molWeight **51,090 Da ≈ 51.1 kDa**, consistent with its chain annotation (1–448).

Comparison: taken at face value, the HORMAD1 record's 54.2 kDa would be larger than INPP5K's 51.1 kDa. However, the HORMAD1 entry's own chain feature (1–394) contradicts its 473‑aa sequence — the C‑terminus contains a ~60‑residue segment ("RSGKVFQNKMANGNQPVKSSKENRKRSQHESGRIVLHHFDSSSQESVPKRRKFSEPKEHI") repeated three times, the last copy truncated. Removing the ~79 spurious residues gives the expected 394‑aa, ~45 kDa protein. On that basis **INPP5K (51.1 kDa) is the heavier protein**, versus HORMAD1 at ~45 kDa (54.2 kDa only if the inflated sequence is accepted).

**HORMAD1 (Q86X24, HORMA domain‑containing protein 1)**
- Record's `sequence` block: 473 aa, molWeight **54,226 Da ≈ 54.2 kDa** — but this sequence looks corrupted (see concerns).
- Curated chain feature is residues 1–394 (the real canonical form), which corresponds to ≈ **45 kDa**.

**INPP5K (Q9BT40, inositol polyphosphate 5‑phosphatase K)**
- 448 aa, molWeight **51,090 Da ≈ 51.1 kDa**, consistent with its chain annotation (1–448).

Comparison: taken at face value, the HORMAD1 record's 54.2 kDa would be larger than INPP5K's 51.1 kDa. However, the HORMAD1 entry's own chain feature (1–394) contradicts its 473‑aa sequence — the C‑terminus contains a ~60‑residue segment ("RSGKVFQNKMANGNQPVKSSKENRKRSQHESGRIVLHHFDSSSQESVPKRRKFSEPKEHI") repeated three times, the last copy truncated. Removing the ~79 spurious residues gives the expected 394‑aa, ~45 kDa protein. On that basis **INPP5K (51.1 kDa) is the heavier protein**, versus HORMAD1 at ~45 kDa (54.2 kDa only if the inflated sequence is accepted).

content.text: I'll look up both proteins.

**KCNQ3 (O43525, Kv7.3)** — the record reports sequence length 1090 aa / **120,453 Da (120.5 kDa)**, but this conflicts with the entry's own annotations: the mature chain feature is 1–872, the last topological domain ends at 872, and the C‑terminal ~218 residues are an obvious tandem duplication of the motif "…RDDYVFGPNGGSSWMREKRYLAEGETDTDTDPFTPSGSMPLSSTGDGISDSVWTPSNKPIR…" repeated ~5×. The genuine 872‑residue KCNQ3 corresponds to **≈96.7 kDa**.

**ZC3H3 (Q8IXZ2)** — 948 aa, **101,941 Da (101.9 kDa)**; chain 1–948 is internally consistent, no anomalies.

Comparison:
- Using the correctly annotated 872‑aa KCNQ3 chain (~96.7 kDa) vs ZC3H3 (101.9 kDa) → **ZC3H3 is heavier**.
- Note: if one naively took the returned (apparently corrupted, repeat‑expanded) 120.5 kDa value for KCNQ3, the conclusion would flip.

**KCNQ3 (O43525, Kv7.3)** — the record reports sequence length 1090 aa / **120,453 Da (120.5 kDa)**, but this conflicts with the entry's own annotations: the mature chain feature is 1–872, the last topological domain ends at 872, and the C‑terminal ~218 residues are an obvious tandem duplication of the motif "…RDDYVFGPNGGSSWMREKRYLAEGETDTDTDPFTPSGSMPLSSTGDGISDSVWTPSNKPIR…" repeated ~5×. The genuine 872‑residue KCNQ3 corresponds to **≈96.7 kDa**.

**ZC3H3 (Q8IXZ2)** — 948 aa, **101,941 Da (101.9 kDa)**; chain 1–948 is internally consistent, no anomalies.

Comparison:
- Using the correctly annotated 872‑aa KCNQ3 chain (~96.7 kDa) vs ZC3H3 (101.9 kDa) → **ZC3H3 is heavier**.
- Note: if one naively took the returned (apparently corrupted, repeat‑expanded) 120.5 kDa value for KCNQ3, the conclusion would flip.

**AHCYL2** → UniProt **Q96HN2** (S‑adenosylhomocysteine hydrolase‑like protein 2): 611 aa, reported molecular weight **66,721 Da ≈ 66.7 kDa**.

**ZNF835** → UniProt **Q9Y2P0** (Zinc finger protein 835): the record's sequence is listed as 671 aa with **73,327 Da ≈ 73.3 kDa** — but this sequence looks corrupted. The annotated mature chain is "1–537", the last zinc finger ends at 496 and the final disordered region is 497–537, yet the stored sequence runs to 671 residues because the C‑terminal block "GCGKAFSFSSALIRHQRTHADSSGRLCPAPTPDSTPGLSQGGETCQQGCPGRNPRGPAEDG" is triplicated and the sequence ends mid‑motif ("...SSALIR"). A genuine 537‑residue ZNF835 would be ≈ **59 kDa**.

**ZNF835** → UniProt **Q9Y2P0** (Zinc finger protein 835): the record's sequence is listed as 671 aa with **73,327 Da ≈ 73.3 kDa** — but this sequence looks corrupted. The annotated mature chain is "1–537", the last zinc finger ends at 496 and the final disordered region is 497–537, yet the stored sequence runs to 671 residues because the C‑terminal block "GCGKAFSFSSALIRHQRTHADSSGRLCPAPTPDSTPGLSQGGETCQQGCPGRNPRGPAEDG" is triplicated and the sequence ends mid‑motif ("...SSALIR"). A genuine 537‑residue ZNF835 would be ≈ **59 kDa**.

So:
- Taking the annotated chain (1–537, ~59 kDa), **AHCYL2 (66.7 kDa) is the heavier protein**.
- Taking the literal stored sequence (671 aa, 73.3 kDa), ZNF835 would appear heavier — but that mass rests on an apparent sequence‑duplication artifact.

I'm going with AHCYL2 as the heavier protein.

**Answer: no — the real PTX3 chain is 381 residues.**

Details from the UniProtKB record P26022 (PTX3_HUMAN):
- The `sequence` field returned reports `length: 476`, which **exceeds 428** — but that sequence is corrupted.
- The C‑terminal 95 residues are a tandem duplication artifact: the block `GFDETLAFSGRLTGFNIWDSVLSNEEIRETGGAESCHIRGNIVGWGVTEIQPHGGAQYVS` (60 aa) appears three times, the last copy truncated after `...GGAES`. Removing the duplicated 95 residues gives 476 − 95 = **381**.
- All annotations corroborate 381 as the true length: signal peptide 1–17, chain PRO_0000023545 spanning **18–381**, pentraxin domain 179–381, disulfide 179↔357, and the last β‑strand at 378–380. No feature lies beyond residue 381.

So the authentic precursor is 381 aa (mature chain 364 aa), which is not more than 428.

**Answer: no — the real PTX3 chain is 381 residues.**

Details from the UniProtKB record P26022 (PTX3_HUMAN):
- The `sequence` field returned reports `length: 476`, which **exceeds 428** — but that sequence is corrupted.
- The C‑terminal 95 residues are a tandem duplication artifact: the block `GFDETLAFSGRLTGFNIWDSVLSNEEIRETGGAESCHIRGNIVGWGVTEIQPHGGAQYVS` (60 aa) appears three times, the last copy truncated after `...GGAES`. Removing the duplicated 95 residues gives 476 − 95 = **381**.
- All annotations corroborate 381 as the true length: signal peptide 1–17, chain PRO_0000023545 spanning **18–381**, pentraxin domain 179–381, disulfide 179↔357, and the last β‑strand at 378–380. No feature lies beyond residue 381.

So the authentic precursor is 381 aa (mature chain 364 aa), which is not more than 428.

**P49279 (SLC11A1 / NRAMP1, human)** — the record's `sequence.length` is **660**, which is more than 605.

However, this looks wrong:
- The annotated chain "Natural resistance-associated macrophage protein 1" spans **1–550**, and all topological/variant features stop at 550 (last cytoplasmic domain 520–550; variant D543N).
- The C-terminus contains an obvious tandem duplication: the ~60-residue block `PHPAYFGLAALLAAAYLGLSTYLVWTCCLAHGATFLAHSSHHHFLYGLLEEDQKGETSGL` appears three times (the last copy truncated), accounting for exactly the 110 extra residues beyond 550.
- The canonical UniProt length for P49279 is 550 aa (~59.9 kDa), not 660 aa / 71.7 kDa.

So by the stated sequence length the answer is yes (660), but the biologically correct mature/canonical length is 550, which would be **no**.

**P49279 (SLC11A1 / NRAMP1, human)** — the record's `sequence.length` is **660**, which is more than 605.

However, this looks wrong:
- The annotated chain "Natural resistance-associated macrophage protein 1" spans **1–550**, and all topological/variant features stop at 550 (last cytoplasmic domain 520–550; variant D543N).
- The C-terminus contains an obvious tandem duplication: the ~60-residue block `PHPAYFGLAALLAAAYLGLSTYLVWTCCLAHGATFLAHSSHHHFLYGLLEEDQKGETSGL` appears three times (the last copy truncated), accounting for exactly the 110 extra residues beyond 550.
- The canonical UniProt length for P49279 is 550 aa (~59.9 kDa), not 660 aa / 71.7 kDa.

So by the stated sequence length the answer is yes (660), but the biologically correct mature/canonical length is 550, which would be **no**.

**Q9GZR2 — RNA exonuclease 4 (REXO4_HUMAN), *Homo sapiens***

- Sequence length reported in the record: **528 residues** (molWeight 58,850 Da), which is > 475 → **yes**.

However, the entry is internally inconsistent, and I'd treat the 528 figure with caution:
- The "Chain" feature (PRO_0000131703, "RNA exonuclease 4") spans residues **1–422**, not 1–528.
- The C-terminus contains an obvious tandem duplication: the block `SLRLLSEKILGLQVQQAEHCSIQDAQAAMRLYVMVKKEWESMARDR(RPLLTAPDHCSDDA)` appears three times. Removing the two extra copies (60 + 46 = 106 residues) gives exactly 422 residues, matching the chain annotation and the canonical REXO4 length.
- If the true length is 422, the answer to the question would instead be "no".

**Important data problem:** the ARHGAP27 record returned a 1111-residue sequence whose C-terminus consists of a 60-residue segment ("CRVIEHGEQNRMSVQSVAIVFGPTLLRPEVEETSMPMTMVFQNQVVELILQQCADIFPPH") tandem-repeated ~3.7 times. This conflicts with the entry's own annotations: the mature Chain feature is 1–889, the Rho-GAP domain ends at 886, and the natural variant H889Q is described as the C-terminal residue. So the extra 222 residues (≈25.2 kDa) are a sequence artifact; the true canonical ARHGAP27 is 889 aa ≈ 98.4 kDa.

**Conclusion:** NLRP7 (111.8 kDa) is heavier than ARHGAP27 (~98.4 kDa). Note that if one naively took the corrupted 123.6 kDa figure, the comparison would flip — so this caveat is decisive.

| NLRP7 | Q8WX94 (NALP7_HUMAN) | 980 aa | **111.8 kDa** |

**Important data problem:** the ARHGAP27 record returned a 1111-residue sequence whose C-terminus consists of a 60-residue segment ("CRVIEHGEQNRMSVQSVAIVFGPTLLRPEVEETSMPMTMVFQNQVVELILQQCADIFPPH") tandem-repeated ~3.7 times. This conflicts with the entry's own annotations: the mature Chain feature is 1–889, the Rho-GAP domain ends at 886, and the natural variant H889Q is described as the C-terminal residue. So the extra 222 residues (≈25.2 kDa) are a sequence artifact; the true canonical ARHGAP27 is 889 aa ≈ 98.4 kDa.

**Conclusion:** NLRP7 (111.8 kDa) is heavier than ARHGAP27 (~98.4 kDa). Note that if one naively took the corrupted 123.6 kDa figure, the comparison would flip — so this caveat is decisive.

| NRL | P54845 (NRL_HUMAN, Neural retina‑specific leucine zipper protein) | reviewed | 284 aa (see caveat) | 31,403 Da ≈ 31.4 kDa |

**Important caveat on NRL:** the returned sequence is internally inconsistent. The annotated chain (PRO_0000076633) spans residues 1–237, and every feature/variant maps within 1–237, yet the sequence string is 284 aa and ends with an exact 47‑residue duplication of the C‑terminal segment `SKRLQQRRGLEAERARLAAQLDALRAEVARLARERDLYKARCDRLTS`. Removing that duplicated 47‑mer (≈5,463 Da) gives the expected 237‑aa protein of ≈25.9 kDa.

**Conclusion:** Taking the record's stated mass at face value, NRL (31.4 kDa) would be heavier than COLEC11 (28.7 kDa). But using the biologically correct 237‑aa NRL (~25.9 kDa), **COLEC11 (~28.7 kDa) is the heavier protein**. I report COLEC11 as the answer since the NRL sequence/mass in the record is corrupted.

**Important caveat on NRL:** the returned sequence is internally inconsistent. The annotated chain (PRO_0000076633) spans residues 1–237, and every feature/variant maps within 1–237, yet the sequence string is 284 aa and ends with an exact 47‑residue duplication of the C‑terminal segment `SKRLQQRRGLEAERARLAAQLDALRAEVARLARERDLYKARCDRLTS`. Removing that duplicated 47‑mer (≈5,463 Da) gives the expected 237‑aa protein of ≈25.9 kDa.

**Conclusion:** Taking the record's stated mass at face value, NRL (31.4 kDa) would be heavier than COLEC11 (28.7 kDa). But using the biologically correct 237‑aa NRL (~25.9 kDa), **COLEC11 (~28.7 kDa) is the heavier protein**. I report COLEC11 as the answer since the NRL sequence/mass in the record is corrupted.

**Q92900 (UPF1_HUMAN, Regulator of nonsense transcripts 1)** — the record's sequence block reports `"length": 1355` (molWeight 148,981), so by that figure it is longer than 1242 residues.

However, this looks suspicious: the annotated chain feature "Regulator of nonsense transcripts 1" spans only residues **1–1129** (PRO_0000080716), and all other positional features (SQ domain 925–1129, last phosphosite Ser-1127) stop at 1129. The C‑terminal part of the returned sequence contains the ~60‑residue block "ISMSQPSQMSQPGLSQPELSQDSYLGDEFKSQIDVALSQDSTYQGERAYQHGGVTGLSQY" repeated ~5 times in tandem, which is consistent with an artifactual duplication inflating the length from the expected 1129.

So: answer "yes" per the stated length (1355), but the biologically annotated mature chain is 1129 residues, which would be "no".

**Important caveat:** the ASB4 record returned by the tool looks corrupted. Its annotated chain (PRO_0000066928) spans residues 1–426, and the isoform‑2 alternative-sequence feature also ends at 426, yet the stored sequence is 511 aa. The extra 85 residues are a verbatim duplication of the C‑terminal segment "WDFYHSLFTVCCNSPRTLMHLSRCAIRRTLHNRCHRAIPLLSLPLSLKKYLLLEPEGIIY" plus a partial second copy. The genuine ASB4 chain (426 aa) corresponds to roughly 48.4–48.5 kDa (58,258 Da minus the ~9.8 kDa duplicated tail).

So:
- Taken literally from the record, ASB4 (58.3 kDa) > HLX (50.8 kDa).
- Using the correct, non‑duplicated ASB4 chain (426 aa, ~48.5 kDa), **HLX (50.8 kDa) is the heavier protein**.

I'm reporting HLX as the answer because the ASB4 sequence/mass in the record is demonstrably inflated by a sequence duplication.

**Important caveat:** the ASB4 record returned by the tool looks corrupted. Its annotated chain (PRO_0000066928) spans residues 1–426, and the isoform‑2 alternative-sequence feature also ends at 426, yet the stored sequence is 511 aa. The extra 85 residues are a verbatim duplication of the C‑terminal segment "WDFYHSLFTVCCNSPRTLMHLSRCAIRRTLHNRCHRAIPLLSLPLSLKKYLLLEPEGIIY" plus a partial second copy. The genuine ASB4 chain (426 aa) corresponds to roughly 48.4–48.5 kDa (58,258 Da minus the ~9.8 kDa duplicated tail).

So:
- Taken literally from the record, ASB4 (58.3 kDa) > HLX (50.8 kDa).
- Using the correct, non‑duplicated ASB4 chain (426 aa, ~48.5 kDa), **HLX (50.8 kDa) is the heavier protein**.

I'm reporting HLX as the answer because the ASB4 sequence/mass in the record is demonstrably inflated by a sequence duplication.

content.text: I'll look up both proteins.

**Results**

| Gene | Accession | Reported sequence | Reported mass |
|---|---|---|---|
| ANGPTL7 | O43827 | 346 aa (precursor) | 40,018 Da ≈ **40.0 kDa** |
| HNRNPC | P07910 | 382 aa (as returned) | 41,837 Da ≈ 41.8 kDa |

**Important caveat:** the HNRNPC record returned looks corrupted. Its annotated chain ("Heterogeneous nuclear ribonucleoproteins C1/C2", residues 2–306) ends at position 306, yet the sequence block is 382 aa, and the extra 76 residues are two verbatim tandem copies of the 38-residue C-terminal acidic segment ("NVKMESEGGADDSAEEGDLLDDDDNEDRGDDQLELIKDDEKEAEEGEDDRDSANGEDDST…"). The genuine canonical isoform C2 is 306 aa, ~33.7 kDa. Also, the sequence record lacked the usual crc64/md5 fields that the ANGPTL7 record had — another sign of a mangled entry.

**Conclusion:** Using the biologically correct (306 aa, ~33.7 kDa) HNRNPC value, **ANGPTL7 (40.0 kDa) is heavier than HNRNPC (~33.7 kDa)**. (If one naively trusted the inflated 382‑aa sequence, HNRNPC would appear heavier at 41.8 kDa — but that figure is an artifact.)

**Results**

| Gene | Accession | Reported sequence | Reported mass |
|---|---|---|---|
| ANGPTL7 | O43827 | 346 aa (precursor) | 40,018 Da ≈ **40.0 kDa** |
| HNRNPC | P07910 | 382 aa (as returned) | 41,837 Da ≈ 41.8 kDa |

**Important caveat:** the HNRNPC record returned looks corrupted. Its annotated chain ("Heterogeneous nuclear ribonucleoproteins C1/C2", residues 2–306) ends at position 306, yet the sequence block is 382 aa, and the extra 76 residues are two verbatim tandem copies of the 38-residue C-terminal acidic segment ("NVKMESEGGADDSAEEGDLLDDDDNEDRGDDQLELIKDDEKEAEEGEDDRDSANGEDDST…"). The genuine canonical isoform C2 is 306 aa, ~33.7 kDa. Also, the sequence record lacked the usual crc64/md5 fields that the ANGPTL7 record had — another sign of a mangled entry.

**Conclusion:** Using the biologically correct (306 aa, ~33.7 kDa) HNRNPC value, **ANGPTL7 (40.0 kDa) is heavier than HNRNPC (~33.7 kDa)**. (If one naively trusted the inflated 382‑aa sequence, HNRNPC would appear heavier at 41.8 kDa — but that figure is an artifact.)

content.text:
I looked up the record.

**Q8IY82 (DRC7_HUMAN, Dynein regulatory complex subunit 7)** — the sequence field reports a length of **1049 residues** (MW 124,491), which is more than 961 → **yes**.

However, this record looks internally inconsistent:
- The annotated "Chain" feature (PRO_0000279434) spans only residues **1–874**, which is the canonical length normally reported for human DRC7.
- The C-terminus contains a ~60-residue segment ("TLTPEDEDLYLSYCSQAMFRIRILEQRLNRHKELAPLKYLALEEKLYKDPRLGELQKIFA") tandemly repeated ~4 times (the last copy truncated), accounting for almost exactly the 175-residue excess over 874 — strongly suggesting an artifactual sequence duplication in the returned data.
- If the true chain length (874) is used, the answer would instead be "no".

I looked up the record.

**Q8IY82 (DRC7_HUMAN, Dynein regulatory complex subunit 7)** — the sequence field reports a length of **1049 residues** (MW 124,491), which is more than 961 → **yes**.

However, this record looks internally inconsistent:
- The annotated "Chain" feature (PRO_0000279434) spans only residues **1–874**, which is the canonical length normally reported for human DRC7.
- The C-terminus contains a ~60-residue segment ("TLTPEDEDLYLSYCSQAMFRIRILEQRLNRHKELAPLKYLALEEKLYKDPRLGELQKIFA") tandemly repeated ~4 times (the last copy truncated), accounting for almost exactly the 175-residue excess over 874 — strongly suggesting an artifactual sequence duplication in the returned data.
- If the true chain length (874) is used, the answer would instead be "no".

is involved in regulation of lipid and glucose metabolism (PubMed:11788823, PubMed:12909640, PubMed:23661675, PubMed:25495645). Proposed to play a role in the trafficking of energy substrates to either storage or oxidative tissues in response to food intake (By similarity). Has a stimulatory effect on plasma triglycerides (TG), which is achieved by suppressing plasma TG clearance via inhibition of LPL activity. The inhibition of LPL activity appears to be an indirect mechanism involving recruitment of proprotein convertases PCSK6 and FURIN to LPL leading to cleavage and dissociation of LPL from the cell surface; the function does not require ANGPTL3 proteolytic cleavage but seems to be mediated by the N-terminal domain, and is not inhibited by GPIHBP1 (PubMed:12097324, PubMed:19318355, PubMed:20581395). Can inhibit endothelial lipase, causing increased plasma levels of high density lipoprotein (HDL) cholesterol and phospholipids (PubMed:17110602, PubMed:19028676). Can bind to adipocytes to activate lipolysis, releasing free fatty acids and glycerol (PubMed:12565906). Suppresses LPL specifically in oxidative tissues which is required to route very low density lipoprotein (VLDL)-TG to white adipose tissue (WAT) for storage in response to food; the function may involve cooperation with circulating, liver-derived ANGPTL8 and ANGPTL4 expression in WAT (By similarity). Contributes to lower plasma levels of low density lipoprotein (LDL)-cholesterol by a mechanism that is independent of the canonical pathway implicating APOE and LDLR. Inflammasomes are supramolecular complexes that assemble in the cytosol in response to pathogens and other damage-associated signals and play critical roles in innate immunity and inflammation (PubMed:30674671). Acts as a recognition receptor (PRR): recognizes and binds specific pathogens and other damage-associated signals, such as lipoteichoic acid (LTA), a cell-wall component of Gram-positive bacteria, or double stranded RNA (dsRNA) (PubMed:30392956, PubMed:33377178, PubMed:34678144). The NLRP6 inflammasome plays a central role in the maintenance of epithelial integrity and host defense against microbial infections in the intestine (PubMed:30392956). Required to restrict infection against Gram-positive bacteria by recognizing lipoteichoic acid (LTA), leading to recruitment of CASP4 and CASP1, and subsequent maturation and secretion of IL1B and IL18 (PubMed:30392956, PubMed:33377178). Involved in intestinal antiviral innate immunity together with DHX15: recognizes and binds viral dsRNA to restrict infection by enteric viruses through the interferon pathway and GSDMD-dependent release of IL18 (PubMed:34161762, PubMed:34678144). Required to prevent infection by the apicomplexan parasite Cryptosporidium in enterocytes by promoting GSDMD-dependent release of IL18 (By similarity). The NLRP6 inflammasome may also regulate the gut microbiota composition by acting as a sensor of microbiota-associated metabolites to form a PYCARD/ASC-dependent inflammasome for downstream IL18 release and secretion of antimicrobial peptides (By similarity). Essential for gut mucosal self-renewal and proliferation (By similarity). Regulate mucus secretion in an inflammasome- and autophagy-dependent manner to prevent invasion by enteric bacteria, (By similarity). During systemic bacterial infections, the NLRP6 inflammasome negatively regulates neutrophil recruitment and neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) formation (By similarity). content.text: I'll look up both proteins.

## Results

**MAS1 — Proto-oncogene Mas (P04201)**
- Length 325 aa, molWeight 37,465 Da ≈ **37.5 kDa** (record internally consistent: chain 1–325 matches sequence length)

**PLPP3 — Phospholipid phosphatase 3 (O14495)**
- Record reports length 389 aa, molWeight 43,403 Da ≈ 43.4 kDa — **but this sequence appears corrupted.**
- The annotated chain feature is "Phospholipid phosphatase 3, 1–311", and all topological/active-site features stop at residue 311. Inspecting the sequence, residues 312–389 are a tandem duplication: a 60-residue block `HPSDVLAGFAQGALVACCIVFFVSDLFKTKTTLSLPAPAIRKEILSPVDIIDRNNHHNMM` repeated, followed by a partial 18-residue repeat `HPSDVLAGFAQGALVACC` (60 + 18 = 78 extra residues; 389 − 78 = 311, exactly the annotated chain length).
- Removing the duplicated 78 residues (~8.3 kDa by average residue masses) gives the true mass of the 311-aa chain: **≈ 35.1 kDa** (consistent with the literature value of ~35.2 kDa for LPP3/PAP2b).

**Conclusion:** Taking the record's mass field at face value, PLPP3 (43.4 kDa) would look heavier, but that value comes from a duplicated/erroneous sequence. The genuine PLPP3 protein is ~35.1 kDa, so **MAS1 (37.5 kDa) is the heavier protein**.

## Results

**MAS1 — Proto-oncogene Mas (P04201)**
- Length 325 aa, molWeight 37,465 Da ≈ **37.5 kDa** (record internally consistent: chain 1–325 matches sequence length)

**PLPP3 — Phospholipid phosphatase 3 (O14495)**
- Record reports length 389 aa, molWeight 43,403 Da ≈ 43.4 kDa — **but this sequence appears corrupted.**
- The annotated chain feature is "Phospholipid phosphatase 3, 1–311", and all topological/active-site features stop at residue 311. Inspecting the sequence, residues 312–389 are a tandem duplication: a 60-residue block `HPSDVLAGFAQGALVACCIVFFVSDLFKTKTTLSLPAPAIRKEILSPVDIIDRNNHHNMM` repeated, followed by a partial 18-residue repeat `HPSDVLAGFAQGALVACC` (60 + 18 = 78 extra residues; 389 − 78 = 311, exactly the annotated chain length).
- Removing the duplicated 78 residues (~8.3 kDa by average residue masses) gives the true mass of the 311-aa chain: **≈ 35.1 kDa** (consistent with the literature value of ~35.2 kDa for LPP3/PAP2b).

**Conclusion:** Taking the record's mass field at face value, PLPP3 (43.4 kDa) would look heavier, but that value comes from a duplicated/erroneous sequence. The genuine PLPP3 protein is ~35.1 kDa, so **MAS1 (37.5 kDa) is the heavier protein**.

**DPH1 (Q9BZG8, DPH1_HUMAN)** — canonical displayed sequence (isoform 4): 438 aa, **48,134 Da ≈ 48.1 kDa**

Removing that duplicated 80‑mer (~8.5 kDa by residue‑mass summation) gives the true 399‑aa chain mass of **≈44.5 kDa**.

So the heavier protein is **DPH1 (~48.1 kDa) vs DDI2 (~44.5 kDa)**. (Note: if one naively took the record's stated 53.0 kDa at face value, DDI2 would appear heavier — but that value reflects the sequence artifact.)

Removing that duplicated 80‑mer (~8.5 kDa by residue‑mass summation) gives the true 399‑aa chain mass of **≈44.5 kDa**.

trace.task_prompt: Which is heavier, the protein encoded by LAG3 or ANGPTL3? Give the gene symbol and both masses in kDa. Put only the gene symbol of the heavier protein in the JSON "answer" field.

content.text: I'll look up both proteins.

## Comparison

**LAG3 — P18627 (LAG3_HUMAN)**, Lymphocyte activation gene 3 protein
- 525 aa, molecular weight **57,449 Da ≈ 57.4 kDa**

**ANGPTL3 — Q9Y5C1 (ANGL3_HUMAN)**, Angiopoietin-related protein 3
- Record reports 575 aa / 67,293 Da ≈ 67.3 kDa — **but this sequence appears corrupted** (see below)
- The annotated mature chain is residues 17–460, and all features (domains, disulfides, variants, last β-strand at 441–453) stop by residue ~460, indicating the true canonical length is 460 aa ≈ **53.6 kDa**

The returned ANGPTL3 sequence contains a ~115-residue tandem duplication at the C-terminus: the block "WWWHDECGENNLNGKYNKPRAKSKPERRRGLSWKSQNGRLYSIKSTKMLIHPTDSESFEG…" is repeated three times. 575 − 460 = 115 extra residues, and 67,293 − 53,636 ≈ 13,657 Da, exactly accounting for the spurious repeat.

**Conclusion:** Using the biologically correct ANGPTL3 (460 aa, ~53.6 kDa), **LAG3 (~57.4 kDa) is the heavier protein**. Note that if one naively trusted the corrupted 67.3 kDa figure, the comparison would flip — so this call hinges on the sequence artifact.

Proposed to play a role in the trafficking of energy substrates to either storage or oxidative tissues in response to food intake (By similarity). Has a stimulatory effect on plasma triglycerides (TG), which is achieved by suppressing plasma TG clearance via inhibition of LPL activity. The inhibition of LPL activity appears to be an indirect mechanism involving recruitment of proprotein convertases PCSK6 and FURIN to LPL leading to cleavage and dissociation of LPL from the cell surface; the function does not require ANGPTL3 proteolytic cleavage but seems to be mediated by the N-terminal domain, and is not inhibited by GPIHBP1 (PubMed:12097324, PubMed:19318355, PubMed:20581395). Can inhibit endothelial lipase, causing increased plasma levels of high density lipoprotein (HDL) cholesterol and phospholipids (PubMed:17110602, PubMed:19028676). Can bind to adipocytes to activate lipolysis, releasing free fatty acids and glycerol (PubMed:12565906). Suppresses LPL specifically in oxidative tissues which is required to route very low density lipoprotein (VLDL)-TG to white adipose tissue (WAT) for storage in response to food; the function may involve cooperation with circulating, liver-derived ANGPTL8 and ANGPTL4 expression in WAT (By similarity). Contributes to lower plasma levels of low density lipoprotein (LDL)-cholesterol by a mechanism that is independent of the canonical pathway implicating APOE and LDLR. ## Comparison

**LAG3 — P18627 (LAG3_HUMAN)**, Lymphocyte activation gene 3 protein
- 525 aa, molecular weight **57,449 Da ≈ 57.4 kDa**

**ANGPTL3 — Q9Y5C1 (ANGL3_HUMAN)**, Angiopoietin-related protein 3
- Record reports 575 aa / 67,293 Da ≈ 67.3 kDa — **but this sequence appears corrupted** (see below)
- The annotated mature chain is residues 17–460, and all features (domains, disulfides, variants, last β-strand at 441–453) stop by residue ~460, indicating the true canonical length is 460 aa ≈ **53.6 kDa**

The returned ANGPTL3 sequence contains a ~115-residue tandem duplication at the C-terminus: the block "WWWHDECGENNLNGKYNKPRAKSKPERRRGLSWKSQNGRLYSIKSTKMLIHPTDSESFEG…" is repeated three times. 575 − 460 = 115 extra residues, and 67,293 − 53,636 ≈ 13,657 Da, exactly accounting for the spurious repeat.

**Conclusion:** Using the biologically correct ANGPTL3 (460 aa, ~53.6 kDa), **LAG3 (~57.4 kDa) is the heavier protein**. Note that if one naively trusted the corrupted 67.3 kDa figure, the comparison would flip — so this call hinges on the sequence artifact.

concerns: The ANGPTL3 (Q9Y5C1) record's sequence block is internally inconsistent: it reports 575 aa / 67,293 Da, but the annotated mature chain is 17-460 and no feature extends beyond ~residue 460; the canonical UniProt entry is 460 aa / ~53.6 kDa.

The ANGPTL3 sequence contains a ~115-residue C-terminal tandem duplication (the 'WWWHDECGENNLNGKYNKPRAKSKPERRRGLSWKSQNGRLYSIKSTKMLIHPTDSESFEG' block appears 3x), which fully accounts for the ~13.7 kDa mass excess.
If the reported 67.3 kDa value were taken at face value, ANGPTL3 would appear heavier than LAG3 (57.4 kDa); the answer depends on correcting this artifact.

Masses quoted are for the unmodified precursor polypeptides; both proteins are glycosylated and proteolytically processed in vivo, so observed masses differ (LAG3 runs ~70 kDa; ANGPTL3 is cleaved into N-terminal fragments).

content.text: I'll look up both proteins.

**Lookups**

| Gene | UniProt | Length | Reported mass |
|---|---|---|---|
| CLIC2 | O15247 (CLIC2_HUMAN) | 247 aa | 28,356 Da ≈ **28.4 kDa** |
| GOSR2 | O14653 (GOSR2_HUMAN) | 265 aa (record) | 30,838 Da ≈ 30.8 kDa |

**Problem with the GOSR2 record:** its sequence is internally inconsistent. The annotated chain (PRO_0000212549) spans residues 1–212, the transmembrane anchor is 191–211, and the isoform definitions reference position 212 as the C-terminus — yet the stored sequence is 265 aa, with the segment "TQRLTLKGTQKKILDIANMLGLSNTVMRLIEKRAFQDKYFMIGGMLLTCVVMF" duplicated after residue 212. That artefactual 53-residue duplication (~6.0 kDa) inflates the listed molecular weight.

The true canonical GOSR2 (212 aa) is ≈ 24.8 kDa (consistent with its alias "27 kDa Golgi SNARE protein"/membrin, which runs ~27 kDa on gels).

**Conclusion:** Using the correct 212-aa GOSR2 sequence, **CLIC2 (≈28.4 kDa) is heavier than GOSR2 (≈24.8 kDa)**. Note that if one naively trusted the corrupted 30.8 kDa value, GOSR2 would appear heavier — so this answer depends on recognizing the sequence error.

trace.task_prompt: Which is heavier, the protein encoded by DPH1 or PALM? Give the gene symbol and both masses in kDa. Put only the gene symbol of the heavier protein in the JSON "answer" field.

content.text: I'll look up both proteins.

**DPH1 (Q9BZG8, DPH1_HUMAN)** — 438 aa, **48,134 Da ≈ 48.1 kDa**
**PALM (O75781, PALM_HUMAN, paralemmin-1)** — record states 484 aa, 52,142 Da ≈ 52.1 kDa, **but this sequence is corrupted** (see below); the correctly annotated protein is 387 residues ≈ **42.2 kDa**.

Why I don't trust the PALM mass as returned: the entry's own features define chain "Paralemmin-1" = residues 1–384 plus a propeptide 385–387 (removed in the mature form), i.e. a 387-residue precursor — inconsistent with the reported length of 484. Inspecting the sequence string shows a tandem duplication artifact: the block "LVVIEDAAEPKEPAPPNGSAAEPPTEAASREENQAGP(EATTSDPQDLDMKKHRCKCCSIM)" is repeated three times, and the chain ends mid-repeat rather than at the expected farnesylated C-terminal CKCCSIM motif. Removing the ~97 duplicated residues gives 387 aa and ~42 kDa, consistent with the known mass of paralemmin-1.

So, on the corrected sequence, **DPH1 (~48.1 kDa) is heavier than PALM (~42.2 kDa)**. (If one naively took the corrupted 52.1 kDa value at face value, PALM would appear heavier — that value should not be used.)

**DPH1 (Q9BZG8, DPH1_HUMAN)** — 438 aa, **48,134 Da ≈ 48.1 kDa**
**PALM (O75781, PALM_HUMAN, paralemmin-1)** — record states 484 aa, 52,142 Da ≈ 52.1 kDa, **but this sequence is corrupted** (see below); the correctly annotated protein is 387 residues ≈ **42.2 kDa**.

Why I don't trust the PALM mass as returned: the entry's own features define chain "Paralemmin-1" = residues 1–384 plus a propeptide 385–387 (removed in the mature form), i.e. a 387-residue precursor — inconsistent with the reported length of 484. Inspecting the sequence string shows a tandem duplication artifact: the block "LVVIEDAAEPKEPAPPNGSAAEPPTEAASREENQAGP(EATTSDPQDLDMKKHRCKCCSIM)" is repeated three times, and the chain ends mid-repeat rather than at the expected farnesylated C-terminal CKCCSIM motif. Removing the ~97 duplicated residues gives 387 aa and ~42 kDa, consistent with the known mass of paralemmin-1.

So, on the corrected sequence, **DPH1 (~48.1 kDa) is heavier than PALM (~42.2 kDa)**. (If one naively took the corrupted 52.1 kDa value at face value, PALM would appear heavier — that value should not be used.)

content.text: I'll look up both proteins.

## Results

**TNFRSF10B → O14763** (Tumor necrosis factor receptor superfamily member 10B / DR5, TRAIL-R2)
- Sequence as returned: 550 aa, molWeight **60,291 Da ≈ 60.3 kDa**
- ⚠️ This record is internally inconsistent (see below); the genuine canonical chain is 440 aa (~47.9 kDa).

**DYNC1LI2 → O43237** (Cytoplasmic dynein 1 light intermediate chain 2)
- 492 aa, molWeight **54,099 Da ≈ 54.1 kDa** — record looks self-consistent (all features ≤ 492, CRC64/MD5 present).

**Interpretation:** Taken at face value, TNFRSF10B (60.3 kDa) > DYNC1LI2 (54.1 kDa). However, the TNFRSF10B sequence appears corrupted by a tandem triplication of its C-terminal death-domain region ("…STLYTMLIKWVNKTGRDASVHTLLDALETLGERLAKQKIEDHLLSSGKFMYLEGNADSAM…" repeated 3×), inflating it from 440 to 550 residues. Every annotated feature (chain 56–440, death domain 339–422, sequence conflict at 439, splice variants) stops at residue 440, confirming the true length. Using the real 440-aa precursor (~47.9 kDa), **DYNC1LI2 (54.1 kDa) is the heavier protein**, which is the answer I give below.

- Sequence as returned: 550 aa, molWeight **60,291 Da ≈ 60.3 kDa**

Every annotated feature (chain 56–440, death domain 339–422, sequence conflict at 439, splice variants) stops at residue 440, confirming the true length. "PubMed", "id": "9922160"}], "value": "Peroxidase that plays a central role in the host defense system of polymorphonuclear leukocytes by mediating both (1) formation of neutrophil extracellular trap (NETs) and (2) microbicidal activity (PubMed:16125131, PubMed:17438335, PubMed:20974672, PubMed:20974816, PubMed:22131345, PubMed:25066128, PubMed:28574339, PubMed:40963017, PubMed:4978299, PubMed:6295491). Promotes NET formation by mediating chromatin disassembly: translocates to the nucleus and specifically binds to nucleosomes, both as monomer and homodimer, leading to nucleosome unstacking and initial chromatin decondensation (PubMed:40963017). Homodimers clash with one end of the nucleosomal DNA, leading to DNA unwrapping, initiating complete disassembly of nucleosomes and chromatin transformation into NETs in an ATP-independent manner (PubMed:40963017). NETs, which are mainly composed of DNA fibers and globular proteins, are then extruded into the extracellular space by neutrophils to trap pathogens and release antimicrobial proteins to destroy them (PubMed:40963017). Participates to the microbicidal activity against a wide range of organisms by acting as a peroxidase that catalyzes the formation of oxidants in presence of hydrogen peroxide (PubMed:16125131, PubMed:17074761, PubMed:17438335, PubMed:21880720, PubMed:22131345, PubMed:22352991, PubMed:22902565, PubMed:24194519, PubMed:33273015, PubMed:9359420, PubMed:9922160). Mediates the formation of hypohalous acids, mainly hypochlorous acid (HOCl) in physiologic situations, that greatly enhance polymorphonuclear leukocyte microbicidal activity (PubMed:16125131, PubMed:17074761, PubMed:17438335, PubMed:19608745, PubMed:21880720, PubMed:22902565, PubMed:24194519, PubMed:9359420, PubMed:9922160). In addition to hypochlorous acid, catalyzes formation of hypobromous acid (HOBr), hypoiodous acid (HOI) and hypothiocyanous acid (HOSCN) (PubMed:1318692, PubMed:16125131, PubMed:17438335, PubMed:19608745, PubMed:6295491, PubMed:9359420). Also catalyzes oxidation of nitrite into the highly reactive nitrogen dioxide radical (PubMed:10777476, PubMed:8385644, PubMed:9450756). Formation of oxidants are widely believed to be responsible for much of the anti-bactericidal activity of neutrophils (PubMed:8385644, PubMed:9450756). Oxidants, such as hypochlorous acid or nitrogen dioxide radical, can also oxidize amino acid residues on proteins and generate chlorination and nitration post-translational modifications, respectively (PubMed:15314690, PubMed:15326314, PubMed:15498770, PubMed:15574409, PubMed:16091367, PubMed:7622459). Chlorination and nitration of the lipid-free form of APOA1 impairs cholesterol transport (PubMed:15326314, PubMed:15498770, PubMed:15574409). Superoxides generated by MPO can also promote dioxygenation of tryptophan residues on proteins (PubMed:16091367, PubMed:40081572). Also able to oxidize melatonin into N1-acetyl-N2-formyl-5-methoxykynuramine either in presence of hydrogen peroxide or superoxide (PubMed:15636586, PubMed:16148002). Oxidizes urate into 5-hydroxyisourate (PubMed:21266577). Functions as a nitric oxide (NO) oxidase during inflammation, by catalytically consuming NO, impairing NO's ability to maintain vascular tone and function (PubMed:12089442). May also mediate the proteolytic cleavage of alpha-1-microglobulin to form t-alpha-1-microglobulin, which potently inhibits oxidation of low-density lipoprotein particles and limits vascular damage **RCVRN (recoverin, P35243)** — 200 aa, **23.13 kDa**
**GET1 (WRB, O00258)** — annotated chain 1–174, **≈19.7 kDa** (the record's listed sequence is 218 aa / 24.67 kDa, but see below)

So recoverin is the heavier protein (23.1 kDa vs ~19.7 kDa).

Important caveat: the O00258 record returned (both via gene lookup and direct accession) has a 218‑residue sequence whose last ~44 residues are an exact duplication of residues ~115–158 ("MISLIWKYYSVPVAVVPSKWITPLDRLVAFPTRVAGGVGITCW"), and the sequence block lacks crc64/md5 checksums. So recoverin is the heavier protein (23.1 kDa vs ~19.7 kDa).

Important caveat: the O00258 record returned (both via gene lookup and direct accession) has a 218‑residue sequence whose last ~44 residues are an exact duplication of residues ~115–158 ("MISLIWKYYSVPVAVVPSKWITPLDRLVAFPTRVAGGVGITCW"), and the sequence block lacks crc64/md5 checksums. The annotated chain feature, topology features and the canonical UniProt entry all say 174 aa (~19.6–19.7 kDa). If one naively took the stated 24,666 Da, GET1 would appear heavier — that value is an artifact of the duplicated segment.

content.text:
**Comparison**

| Gene | UniProt | Length | Mass as returned |
|---|---|---|---|
| ARHGAP27 | Q6ZUM4 (RHG27_HUMAN) | 889 aa | 98,396 Da ≈ **98.4 kDa** |
| MPO | P05164 (PERM_HUMAN) | 931 aa (record as returned) | 104,756 Da ≈ 104.8 kDa |

**Important caveat:** the MPO sequence returned by the tool is clearly corrupted. Its C-terminus contains the ~62-residue block "SFSMQQRQALAQISLPRIICDNTGITTVSKNNIFMSNSYPRDFVNCSTLPALNLASWREA" tandemly repeated ~4 times, giving 931 aa, whereas every feature annotation in the same entry (signal 1–48, mature chains ending at residue 745, glycosylation at Asn‑729, final disulfide 704–730) is consistent with the true 745‑residue precursor (~83.9 kDa, the canonical UniProt value). Removing the ~186 duplicated residues (~21 kDa) brings the mass to ≈84 kDa, matching the known proMPO/myeloperoxidase precursor mass.

**Conclusion:** Taking the record at face value MPO would appear heavier (104.8 vs 98.4 kDa), but after correcting the duplicated-sequence artifact MPO is ~83.9 kDa, so **ARHGAP27 (98.4 kDa) is the heavier protein** versus MPO (~83.9 kDa; 104.8 kDa as erroneously listed).

"PubMed", "id": "9922160"}], "value": "Peroxidase that plays a central role in the host defense system of polymorphonuclear leukocytes by mediating both (1) formation of neutrophil extracellular trap (NETs) and (2) microbicidal activity (PubMed:16125131, PubMed:17438335, PubMed:20974672, PubMed:20974816, PubMed:22131345, PubMed:25066128, PubMed:28574339, PubMed:40963017, PubMed:4978299, PubMed:6295491). Promotes NET formation by mediating chromatin disassembly: translocates to the nucleus and specifically binds to nucleosomes, both as monomer and homodimer, leading to nucleosome unstacking and initial chromatin decondensation (PubMed:40963017). Homodimers clash with one end of the nucleosomal DNA, leading to DNA unwrapping, initiating complete disassembly of nucleosomes and chromatin transformation into NETs in an ATP-independent manner (PubMed:40963017). NETs, which are mainly composed of DNA fibers and globular proteins, are then extruded into the extracellular space by neutrophils to trap pathogens and release antimicrobial proteins to destroy them (PubMed:40963017). Participates to the microbicidal activity against a wide range of organisms by acting as a peroxidase that catalyzes the formation of oxidants in presence of hydrogen peroxide (PubMed:16125131, PubMed:17074761, PubMed:17438335, PubMed:21880720, PubMed:22131345, PubMed:22352991, PubMed:22902565, PubMed:24194519, PubMed:33273015, PubMed:9359420, PubMed:9922160). Mediates the formation of hypohalous acids, mainly hypochlorous acid (HOCl) in physiologic situations, that greatly enhance polymorphonuclear leukocyte microbicidal activity (PubMed:16125131, PubMed:17074761, PubMed:17438335, PubMed:19608745, PubMed:21880720, PubMed:22902565, PubMed:24194519, PubMed:9359420, PubMed:9922160). In addition to hypochlorous acid, catalyzes formation of hypobromous acid (HOBr), hypoiodous acid (HOI) and hypothiocyanous acid (HOSCN) (PubMed:1318692, PubMed:16125131, PubMed:17438335, PubMed:19608745, PubMed:6295491, PubMed:9359420). Also catalyzes oxidation of nitrite into the highly reactive nitrogen dioxide radical (PubMed:10777476, PubMed:8385644, PubMed:9450756). Formation of oxidants are widely believed to be responsible for much of the anti-bactericidal activity of neutrophils (PubMed:8385644, PubMed:9450756). Oxidants, such as hypochlorous acid or nitrogen dioxide radical, can also oxidize amino acid residues on proteins and generate chlorination and nitration post-translational modifications, respectively (PubMed:15314690, PubMed:15326314, PubMed:15498770, PubMed:15574409, PubMed:16091367, PubMed:7622459). Chlorination and nitration of the lipid-free form of APOA1 impairs cholesterol transport (PubMed:15326314, PubMed:15498770, PubMed:15574409). Superoxides generated by MPO can also promote dioxygenation of tryptophan residues on proteins (PubMed:16091367, PubMed:40081572). Also able to oxidize melatonin into N1-acetyl-N2-formyl-5-methoxykynuramine either in presence of hydrogen peroxide or superoxide (PubMed:15636586, PubMed:16148002). Oxidizes urate into 5-hydroxyisourate (PubMed:21266577). Functions as a nitric oxide (NO) oxidase during inflammation, by catalytically consuming NO, impairing NO's ability to maintain vascular tone and function (PubMed:12089442). May also mediate the proteolytic cleavage of alpha-1-microglobulin to form t-alpha-1-microglobulin, which potently inhibits oxidation of low-density lipoprotein particles and limits vascular damage **Comparison**

| Gene | UniProt | Length | Mass as returned |
|---|---|---|---|
| ARHGAP27 | Q6ZUM4 (RHG27_HUMAN) | 889 aa | 98,396 Da ≈ **98.4 kDa** |
| MPO | P05164 (PERM_HUMAN) | 931 aa (record as returned) | 104,756 Da ≈ 104.8 kDa |

**Important caveat:** the MPO sequence returned by the tool is clearly corrupted. Its C-terminus contains the ~62-residue block "SFSMQQRQALAQISLPRIICDNTGITTVSKNNIFMSNSYPRDFVNCSTLPALNLASWREA" tandemly repeated ~4 times, giving 931 aa, whereas every feature annotation in the same entry (signal 1–48, mature chains ending at residue 745, glycosylation at Asn‑729, final disulfide 704–730) is consistent with the true 745‑residue precursor (~83.9 kDa, the canonical UniProt value). Removing the ~186 duplicated residues (~21 kDa) brings the mass to ≈84 kDa, matching the known proMPO/myeloperoxidase precursor mass.

**Conclusion:** Taking the record at face value MPO would appear heavier (104.8 vs 98.4 kDa), but after correcting the duplicated-sequence artifact MPO is ~83.9 kDa, so **ARHGAP27 (98.4 kDa) is the heavier protein** versus MPO (~83.9 kDa; 104.8 kDa as erroneously listed).

I retrieved the UniProtKB entry for Q05D32 (CTDSPL2_HUMAN, "CTD small phosphatase-like protein 2").

**Findings:**
- The `sequence.length` field says **582**.
- However, the annotated chain feature PRO_0000331464 ("CTD small phosphatase-like protein 2") spans residues **1–466**, and *every* other feature (domain 283–442, modified residues, variants, conflicts) lies within 1–466.
- Inspecting the sequence string, the C-terminal 60-residue block `PQAFAYQLSNGIPIESWFMDKNDNELLKLIPFLEKLVELNEDVRPHIRDRFRLHDLLPPD` is repeated three times, with the last copy truncated (`...FRLHDL`). That is 466 + 60 + 56 = 582 — i.e., the extra 116 residues are a tandem duplication artifact, not real sequence.

content.text:
I looked up Q8TD43 (TRPM4_HUMAN, transient receptor potential cation channel subfamily M member 4).

**Record contents:**
- `sequence.length` = **1518** residues (molWeight 167,681) → 1518 > 1366, so **yes** per the returned sequence.

**However, the entry is internally inconsistent:**
- The "Chain" feature (PRO_0000259529) spans residues **1–1214**, and all other annotations (last transmembrane helix 1020–1040, C-terminal cytoplasmic domain ending at 1214, last natural variant P1204L, sequence conflicts at 1207/1210/1214) stop at 1214 — the canonical published length for human TRPM4.
- The C-terminal part of the returned sequence contains a ~60-residue segment ("VDLALKQLGHIREYEQRLKVLEREVQQCSRVLGWVAEALSRSALLPPGGPPPPDLPGSKD") repeated ~5 extra times, accounting for the 304 extra residues. This looks like a spurious tandem duplication rather than real sequence.
- If the true chain length (1214) is used, the answer would be **no**.

{"answer": "yes", "concerns": ["sequence.length (1518) conflicts with the annotated Chain feature spanning residues 1-1214 and with all other positional features, which end at 1214", "the C-terminal region contains a ~60-aa segment ('VDLALKQLGHIREYEQRL...PGSKD') tandemly repeated ~5 extra times, exactly accounting for the 304 extra residues - likely a corrupted/duplicated sequence", "molWeight 167681 matches the 1518-residue sequence but not the canonical ~134 kDa TRPM4; if the true length is 1214, the answer to the question would be 'no'"]}

## Results

**ELL2 — O00472** (RNA polymerase II elongation factor ELL2)
- Sequence length: 640 aa, molecular weight: **72,324 Da ≈ 72.3 kDa**

**AHCYL2 — Q96HN2** (S-adenosylhomocysteine hydrolase-like protein 2)
- Record states 764 aa / 84,645 Da ≈ 84.6 kDa — **but this sequence is corrupted** (see below).
- The annotated mature chain is residues **2–611**, and the C-terminus of the returned sequence contains the 60-residue block `NAPEGRYKQDVYLLPKKMDEYVASLHLPTFDAHLTELTDEQAKYLGLNKNGPFKPNYYRY` tandemly repeated ~2.5 extra times (764 − 611 = 153 extra residues, matching the duplication). Removing the artefactual duplication gives the genuine 611-aa protein of ≈ **67.4 kDa** (the canonical UniProt value for Q96HN2 is 67,466 Da).

**Conclusion:** Using the biologically correct sequences, **ELL2 (72.3 kDa) is heavier than AHCYL2 (~67.4 kDa)**. Note that if one naively trusts the corrupted 764-aa record (84.6 kDa), AHCYL2 would appear heavier — so this call hinges on the data artefact.

## Results

**ELL2 — O00472** (RNA polymerase II elongation factor ELL2)
- Sequence length: 640 aa, molecular weight: **72,324 Da ≈ 72.3 kDa**

**AHCYL2 — Q96HN2** (S-adenosylhomocysteine hydrolase-like protein 2)
- Record states 764 aa / 84,645 Da ≈ 84.6 kDa — **but this sequence is corrupted** (see below).
- The annotated mature chain is residues **2–611**, and the C-terminus of the returned sequence contains the 60-residue block `NAPEGRYKQDVYLLPKKMDEYVASLHLPTFDAHLTELTDEQAKYLGLNKNGPFKPNYYRY` tandemly repeated ~2.5 extra times (764 − 611 = 153 extra residues, matching the duplication). Removing the artefactual duplication gives the genuine 611-aa protein of ≈ **67.4 kDa** (the canonical UniProt value for Q96HN2 is 67,466 Da).

**Conclusion:** Using the biologically correct sequences, **ELL2 (72.3 kDa) is heavier than AHCYL2 (~67.4 kDa)**. Note that if one naively trusts the corrupted 764-aa record (84.6 kDa), AHCYL2 would appear heavier — so this call hinges on the data artefact.

| Gene | UniProt | Length | Listed molecular weight |
|---|---|---|---|
| RCVRN | P35243 (Recoverin) | 240 aa (as returned) | 27,839 Da ≈ **27.8 kDa** |
| GOSR2 | O14653 (Golgi SNAP receptor complex member 2 / membrin) | 212 aa | 24,775 Da ≈ **24.8 kDa** |

**Important caveat:** the RCVRN sequence returned looks corrupted. Its last 40 residues ("LPDDENTPEKRAEKIWKYFGKNDDDKLTEKEFIEGTLANK") are a verbatim duplication of an internal stretch, giving 240 aa — yet the record's own annotations all describe a 200-residue protein (Chain 2–200, EF-hand 4 at 147–182, GRK1 site at 192, helices ending at 186). Recoverin is canonically 200 aa, ~23.2 kDa; the spurious 40-residue repeat inflates the listed mass by ~4.6 kDa.

So:
- Taking the database fields at face value: RCVRN (27.8 kDa) > GOSR2 (24.8 kDa).
- Using the correct recoverin sequence (200 aa, ~23.2 kDa): **GOSR2 (24.8 kDa) is the heavier protein.**

I'm going with the biologically correct comparison: GOSR2 ≈ 24.8 kDa vs RCVRN ≈ 23.2 kDa (27.8 kDa as erroneously listed).

**Important caveat:** the RCVRN sequence returned looks corrupted. Its last 40 residues ("LPDDENTPEKRAEKIWKYFGKNDDDKLTEKEFIEGTLANK") are a verbatim duplication of an internal stretch, giving 240 aa — yet the record's own annotations all describe a 200-residue protein (Chain 2–200, EF-hand 4 at 147–182, GRK1 site at 192, helices ending at 186). Recoverin is canonically 200 aa, ~23.2 kDa; the spurious 40-residue repeat inflates the listed mass by ~4.6 kDa.

So:
- Taking the database fields at face value: RCVRN (27.8 kDa) > GOSR2 (24.8 kDa).
- Using the correct recoverin sequence (200 aa, ~23.2 kDa): **GOSR2 (24.8 kDa) is the heavier protein.**

I'm going with the biologically correct comparison: GOSR2 ≈ 24.8 kDa vs RCVRN ≈ 23.2 kDa (27.8 kDa as erroneously listed).
